punchline: Lincoln began his militia service as a captain and ended it as a private, and Maxwell says the rank was never the leadership.
thirty_sec: In Maxwell's retelling, young Lincoln raised a militia company and became captain by custom. At a gate he forgot the right command and shouted that the company was dismissed for two minutes, to fall in on the other side. His influence slipped, and he ended as a private. Maxwell's point: a rank can be handed to you, but influence has to be earned.
